lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Do not put that file in a queue. The land is worth one crore forty lakh, and I need an order by Friday.
lines.sfx_cue: heavy file dragged across wooden desk

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, he walked straight inside. I told him there is a registry process.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is. Sit down, both of you.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: I prefer standing. The seller took two lakh from me, signed an agreement, and now wants to sell elsewhere.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: What do you want from this forum?

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Specific performance. Possession. Registration at the agreed price of thirty-one lakh.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You said the land is worth one crore forty lakh.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: That is why Friday is important.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. Notice must be served. The other party must consent to arbitration.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: The agreement contains an arbitration clause.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: An arbitration clause is not consent to whichever room you choose.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Then persuade him this is the correct room.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I do not persuade parties. I hear them.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Of course. Your shop is above rented premises, isn't it? A long dispute with the landlord would be inconvenient.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir... should I go outside?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. You are the registry clerk. Record that the applicant requested an urgent hearing.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What case number?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Case number zero zero three of two thousand twenty-two.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Friday, eleven in the morning.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You will not fix my hearing.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Certainly not, sir. I will merely bring everybody at the useful time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Friday arrived with two witnesses, one reluctant seller, and an advocate old enough to distrust clean paper.
lines.sfx_cue: tyre shop air compressor roaring below

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Case number zero zero three of two thousand twenty-two. Applicant versus respondent. All parties come inside.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: This is the court? Above a tyre shop?

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Do not answer anything yet. Let me see the board.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: You received notice. You came with counsel. Please do not waste the presiding officer's time.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Presiding over what?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Counsel, take your seat.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I have practised for thirty-eight years. I stand until I know before whom I am appearing.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then remain standing and read clause fourteen of your client's agreement.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I have read it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Read it aloud.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Any dispute arising from this agreement shall be referred to arbitration by a sole arbitrator mutually accepted by both parties.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Good. Is your client disputing the agreement?

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: I dispute the price. Thirty-one lakh is robbery now.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: It was not robbery when he took my two lakh.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: That was a token. I... I said I would return it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did you return it?

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did you send written cancellation?

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did you accept another offer?

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Sir, that question concerns a separate negotiation.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then the answer is yes.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: They offered ninety-eight lakh.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: There. He admits it.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: He admits receiving an offer. He does not admit this forum has jurisdiction.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your client came after notice. He filed a reply through you. He is arguing the merits.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Appearance is not appointment.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Correct. Sarika, give both parties the consent memorandum.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, the blue copy or the white copy?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The white copy. Blue remains in registry.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: You prepared consent forms before we entered?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: A competent registry prepares for foreseeable objections.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: What happens if I do not sign?

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Then the advance dispute continues, the other purchaser waits, and your title remains questioned.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Do not instruct my client.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Counsel, advise him. I will give you ten minutes.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: And if we sign, you will hear us fully?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Every document. Every objection. On record.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I want that sentence written into the memorandum.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Sarika, add it.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Every document and... every objection will be heard on record.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Now leave them space to decide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ten minutes became twenty-three. Then the old advocate returned with both signatures.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: My client consents to this arbitration. That is not an admission on the merits.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Recorded. Now show me why an agreement taken for thirty-one lakh should disappear when the value rises.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Because the applicant was required to pay the balance within sixty days.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did he offer payment?

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: He sent three letters.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: And a banker's cheque for twenty-nine lakh.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: I did not deposit it.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That was your choice. His obligation was to tender payment.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: The agreement also required title clearance.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Which your client delayed by withholding the original property card.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: Who told you that?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your own reply. Paragraph nine.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I... let me see that.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You drafted it.

lines.speaker: voice in room
lines.text: The advocate wrote against his own client.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Silence. This is not a tea stall.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No. It is a hearing. Continue with your objection.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: There is no further factual objection.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then the hearing is closed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For forty minutes, Morris typed the largest order he had ever put beneath his seal.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The respondent shall accept the balance of twenty-nine lakh and execute the conveyance within seven days.
lines.sfx_cue: room silent under tyre shop rumble

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Until registration, the respondent shall create no third-party interest in the land.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: And if I refuse?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your signed consent and this award will accompany the applicant's enforcement petition.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: I have the banker's cheque here.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Give it to me. My client will acknowledge receipt.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: You are telling me to obey him? In front of everyone?

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I am telling you that you signed the agreement, accepted arbitration, and lost on the documents.

lines.speaker: landowner
lines.text: Then write that I am taking the cheque under the award.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I will record it, sir.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Record this also. My client will execute the conveyance within seven days.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Thank you, sir. A useful order, exactly when required.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The order follows the record, not your requirement.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: One matter remains.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: What matter?

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: May I see the order appointing you as arbitrator?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The parties appointed me by signing the consent memorandum. You watched them sign it.
lines.sfx_cue: ceiling fan clicking over a silent room

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I watched them consent today. I asked for the order that placed you here before today.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Counsel, your client accepted the award. Do not manufacture dignity after losing.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: I am not speaking to you.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: There is no prior appointment order. This was an ad hoc reference by consent.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Then remove the court emblem from your seal.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: It is not a court emblem. Sir said it is a forum seal.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Young woman, do you know the difference?

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I... I maintain the registry. I do not design seals.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Address me, counsel. Not my staff.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Very well. Your award holds because my client signed, accepted the cheque, and will obey it.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: The next lawyer may ask questions before his client signs anything.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The next lawyer may read his file before entering my room.

lines.speaker: advocate
lines.text: Perhaps. Keep your appointment papers ready anyway.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Do you have a problem?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your matter is concluded.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: That was not my question.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Take your certified copy tomorrow.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: A room like this should know which disputes are safe before the parties arrive.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Safe for whom?

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: For the dignity of the chair, naturally.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Go downstairs.

lines.speaker: dhawale
lines.text: Certainly, sir. My conveyance is on Tuesday. I trust the certified copy will look official.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, should I change the seal?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Should I make an appointment file?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Then what should I do?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Prepare the certified copy. Two sets. Bind the consent memorandum before the award.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: And case number zero zero four? Two people are waiting outside.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Send them away.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: They paid the filing fee.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Refund it.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, did they do something wrong?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Their dispute is already in district court. If we touch it, someone will compare the files.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: How will we know that before reading every file?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: We will know.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That evening, Morris returned to the real court where he still earned money typing other men's orders.
lines.sfx_cue: court copying room printers and stamp pads

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: The copying section closes at six.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I need five minutes with the civil pending register.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Then you need the civil registry, not me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The civil registry sent the list for photocopying this afternoon.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Many things come here. Many things leave.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: This one is thirty-two pages, stapled in three sections, with tomorrow's cause-list changes attached.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: You notice a great deal for a typist.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I was not always a typist.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Yes. Everyone remembers what you were.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I need to check four names. Nothing more.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: File an inspection application.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That creates an entry.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Entries are the purpose of a registry.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Not every glance needs a record.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: In this building, every useful glance does.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Five hundred rupees.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Put your money away.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: One thousand.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: If I wanted notes, I would not negotiate beside a government photocopier.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then tell me what you want.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Today, I want to close the grille.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The next evening, Morris returned. The evening after that, he returned again.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: You are making my tea cold.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And you are still taking the pending list into the copying room at five forty.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Official work has a schedule.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Leave it on the rear machine for two minutes.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: So I can avoid matters already before the court.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Avoid them where?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: In private dispute work.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Private work with case numbers?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Case numbers organise paper.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Private work with a registry clerk?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Staff organise people.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Private work with certified copies?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You have been asking about me.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: No. People carry interesting paper into photocopy shops without being asked.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Have you seen one of my orders?

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: I saw enough to understand why you need my list.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: And why is that?

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: You cannot afford a real judge to see two proceedings for the same dispute.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The parties consent to private arbitration.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Then file the awards properly.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I asked for names, not advice.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: And I refused money, not conversation.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: What conversation do you want?

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Not here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the sixth evening, the rear photocopier held thirty-two pages with no clerk beside them.
lines.sfx_cue: photocopier warming up in empty room

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Civil suits. Land references. Maintenance applications. Execution matters.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: No flash.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You said two minutes.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: One minute remains.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: How often is this list issued?

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Every working day. Changes come in red pencil.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I need it twice a week.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: You need it every day. A petition can be filed between your notice and your hearing.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Every day, then.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: The rear machine will be unattended at five forty-five.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: For how much?

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: I already refused your cash.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Nothing is free in this building.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: Correct.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Name your price.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: My price is not money.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: One sealed envelope every month. You will open it first.

lines.speaker: pandit
lines.text: No questions.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: No court has made me answer her in eleven years. This room above a tyre shop will not be the first.
lines.sfx_cue: legal notice slapped onto wooden desk

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: You came because the notice frightened you.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I came to see which fool stamped it.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Do not speak like that before the presiding officer.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Presiding officer of what?
lines.sfx_cue: plastic chairs scraping, lane voices outside

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Sit down.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I will stand.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then you will stand quietly while your sister speaks.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Sir, he has the keys to my father's western field and the storage room. He has kept them since the funeral.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I kept the land alive. She married and left.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: I became a widow and returned. You still would not let me enter.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Because you returned with debts.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: My debts do not erase my name from the property card.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Show me the property card.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Here. Certified copy. My name and his name, equal shares.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: When did you obtain this copy?

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Yesterday. I waited four hours at the land records counter.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: A name on paper does not harvest groundnuts.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Do you dispute that she owns half?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I paid the tax. I repaired the well. I paid for our father's funeral.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: That was not my question.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I... I do not dispute the name. I dispute what she deserves.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Eleven years of crop income. I deserve accounts also.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: This hearing is not today.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Sir, please. He is bringing a tenant in eight days.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: A lawful tenant. He will cultivate the western side.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: My side.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Nothing is divided.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Hear us before he gives possession. I have waited eleven years. I cannot wait another month.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Eight days is not enough for notice, reply, documents and evidence.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Then tell me how many more years are proper.

lines.speaker: voice in room
lines.text: She has a point, sir.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: This is family business. These people should leave.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You called this room foolish in front of them. You may answer in front of them.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I want a lawyer.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Bring one. The hearing is in eight days at ten thirty.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Case number zero one one of two thousand twenty-two.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Zero one one? How many people have come here?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Enough to know when a man is delaying his sister.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I will return with every receipt.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Bring the keys also.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: You will not touch them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For eight days, Sarika numbered receipts while Morris compared them against the property record.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Land tax, seven years. Well repair, eighteen thousand. Funeral expenses, forty-six thousand.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Separate expenses that preserve the property from expenses Bhaskar owed as a son.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: How do I know the difference?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You do not decide. You make two lists.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, Manjula has no crop receipts.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Because Bhaskar sold the crops.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Then how can she prove the amount?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: He must disclose it.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: What if he does not?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Then his silence will cost him.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir... is that written in a rule?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: It is written in the way evidence works.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: I will prepare both lists.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the eighth morning, Bhaskar returned without a lawyer and with a cloth bag full of receipts.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Case number zero one one of two thousand twenty-two. Both parties are present.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Bhaskar, did you bring the tenancy agreement?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I did not sign it.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Because the notice stopped you.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Because I chose to wait.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Good. The land remains unencumbered. Now, your accounts.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Every expense is in that bag.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Expenses are not accounts. How much crop did you sell last year?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: There was little rain.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Maybe sixty thousand.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: The trader told me one lakh twelve thousand.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: The trader lies.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Did he pay by bank transfer?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Some transfer. Some cash.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Your statement shows eighty-four thousand from him in three payments.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: That included the previous balance.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Which previous balance?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I do not... I do not remember.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: For eleven years, you remembered every rupee you spent. You forgot only what you received.

lines.speaker: voice in room
lines.text: He remembers the keys well enough.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: They are laughing because you are humiliating me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: You humiliated your sister at the gate of her own land. I am asking for figures.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Ask him about the storage room. My father's tools are still inside.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Bhaskar, who owns those tools?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: We both do.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Who has access?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I have the keys.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: So your sister owns half the tools, half the land, and none of the access.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: She could have asked properly.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: I asked at the funeral. I asked at the first harvest. I asked after my husband died.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: You told me a married daughter enters only as a guest.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I was angry.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: For eleven years?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Enough. The documents are complete.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: You cannot divide agricultural land from this table.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I am not changing the revenue boundary. I am ordering access and possession according to recorded ownership.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: What about my expenses?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Proven preservation expenses will be adjusted against crop income. You will submit complete accounts within thirty days.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: And until then?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Until then, you will not lease, sell or obstruct the western half.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: And the keys?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: The keys will be delivered within twenty-four hours.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: You have already written the judgment.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: I wrote it after reading what you brought.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: If I refuse, will police come?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: If you refuse, your sister will carry this signed judgment wherever enforcement is required.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Let me read it.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Take your time. The operative directions are on the last page.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: No tenancy. Equal access. Accounts in thirty days. Keys in twenty-four hours.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Say whether you will obey it.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Do not command me.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: She is not commanding you. The judgment is.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Everyone outside will say I lost to my younger sister.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Everyone outside already knows you kept her land for eleven years.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: You wanted the keys. Take them.
lines.sfx_cue: key ring dropped into an open palm

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: The small brass key is for the storage room?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: And the black key?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: The western gate.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: You are giving both under the judgment?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I read it. I folded it. I am obeying it.

lines.speaker: voice in room
lines.text: Say that louder. We could not hear you at the back.

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: I said I am obeying the court's judgment.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Sir, should I record delivery of the keys?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: Record the time and obtain both signatures.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: My hand is shaking. Show me where to sign.

lines.speaker: sarika
lines.text: Here. Below the words, possession acknowledged.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before noon, the western gate opened for the first time in eleven years.
lines.sfx_cue: rusted padlock opening, metal gate creaking

lines.speaker: lane woman
lines.text: Manjula, where did you get those keys?

lines.speaker: lane man
lines.text: Did your brother finally give them?

lines.speaker: bhaskar
lines.text: Do not make a procession of this.

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: You made me beg at this gate for eleven years. Today, they will all hear.

lines.speaker: lane woman
lines.text: Who gave the order?

lines.speaker: manjula
lines.text: Listen, all of you. A court finally listened to me.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Dhawale brought a land dispute concerning property valued at one crore forty lakh and pressed Morris for an urgent ruling.

state_changes.fact: placed a high-value land dispute before Morris
accepted his largest matter to date for hearing

beat_sheet.what_happened: The landowner appeared with the advocate, signed a consent memorandum and argued the land dispute before Morris.

state_changes.fact: observed Morris conduct a high-value hearing under a signed consent memorandum
recorded the parties' consent and proceedings

beat_sheet.what_happened: Morris ordered conveyance at the contracted price, and the landowner accepted the balance payment while the advocate stated that his client would comply.

state_changes.fact: issued an award that the losing party publicly agreed to obey
secured an enforceable signed resolution for the land purchase
acknowledged that the ruling held because his client had consented and accepted payment

beat_sheet.what_happened: A copy of the signed consent memorandum and award was preserved with the land transaction papers.

state_changes.fact: now contains documentary evidence of Morris's award

beat_sheet.note: No cast character perceived the records handling, leaving the location and future path of the preserved copy open.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Morris admitted there was no prior appointment order, and the advocate warned that another lawyer could challenge the room before consenting.

state_changes.fact: recognized that comparison with formal court records could expose his forum
learned that Morris had no prior appointment order for the matter

beat_sheet.what_happened: Morris asked Pandit for access to the civil pending list so he could avoid disputes already filed in the real court, and Pandit refused cash.

state_changes.fact: learned why Morris needed the pending list
sought confidential registry information to screen future cases

beat_sheet.what_happened: Pandit left the pending list on a rear photocopier long enough for Morris to photograph all thirty-two pages.

state_changes.fact: obtained the real court's current pending list
began leaking confidential registry information to Morris

beat_sheet.what_happened: Pandit demanded one sealed envelope each month, to be opened by Morris without questions, as the price of continued access.

state_changes.fact: made continued leaks conditional on a monthly sealed envelope
became indebted to Pandit on undisclosed terms

beat_sheet.what_happened: Manjula sought an urgent hearing over land and keys withheld by Bhaskar for eleven years, and Morris fixed the hearing for eight days later.

state_changes.fact: obtained a hearing before Bhaskar could place a tenant on the land
was required to answer his sister's claim publicly

beat_sheet.what_happened: At the hearing, Morris established that Manjula held an equal recorded share while Bhaskar controlled all access and had not fully accounted for crop income.

state_changes.fact: failed to justify excluding Manjula from jointly recorded property
proved her recorded ownership and lack of access

beat_sheet.what_happened: Morris awarded Manjula access and possession according to her recorded share, barred Bhaskar from leasing the western half and ordered delivery of the keys.

state_changes.fact: received judgment granting access and possession of her share
was ordered to surrender the keys and provide accounts
issued a judgment that protected Manjula's recorded ownership

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bhaskar delivered both keys under the judgment, and Manjula publicly told the lane that a court had finally listened to her.

state_changes.fact: gained physical access to the land and storage room after eleven years
publicly acknowledged that he was obeying the court's judgment
had a second ruling obeyed outside his hearing room
